data.title: Bootkit / Pre-OS Persistence Hijack
data.summary: The sample replaces or patches boot-chain components — the MBR, bootloader, or UEFI firmware — so its code runs before the operating system, and before most security tooling, loads.
data.description:
Executing ahead of the OS is the whole point: a bootkit can disable or patch the security
controls the OS would otherwise start, and survives a straightforward OS reinstall that
does not also rewrite the boot chain. UEFI variants, in particular, can persist through a
full disk wipe if they live in flash rather than on the drive itself, which changes the
remediation calculus from 'reimage' to 'reflash firmware, then reimage'.
data.recommendation:
* Verify boot-chain integrity (Secure Boot status, bootloader hash, UEFI firmware version/hash) against a known-good baseline, not just the OS volume.
* Where UEFI compromise is suspected, reflash firmware from a trusted source before reimaging — a disk wipe alone will not remove it.
* Enable Secure Boot and firmware write-protection as a baseline control; this class of persistence depends on being able to write to the boot chain in the first place.
data.short_recommendation: Verify boot-chain and firmware integrity directly; reimaging the OS volume alone will not remove this.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Overwrote the master boot record with a loader that patched kernel initialisation before the OS's own drivers loaded.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Patched the master boot record to load the payload ahead of the operating system kernel.
